passage: Honestly, I'm not proud of this. I'm Shankar, and last month when Lokesh chose football practice over my birthday plan, I went silent. I left his messages on read for two days and answered "It's fine" in a tone that meant it wasn't. When he apologised, I said "You obviously don't care." He kept saying sorry, and that felt powerful for about an hour. Then it felt like a stone in my stomach, because I'd wanted him to guess my hurt instead of just saying I was sad. Lokesh looked tired at school, like he was walking on eggshells. That's when I saw the pattern. I told him, "I've been punishing you with silence. That was wrong and I'm sorry. Next time I'll say what I want." He didn't say much, just nodded.

qa.q: How long did Shankar leave Lokesh's messages on read?
qa.a: Shankar left them on read for two days.

qa.q: What did Shankar feel after Lokesh kept apologising?
qa.a: At first Shankar felt powerful for about an hour, and then guilt like a stone in the stomach, because Shankar had wanted the hurt to be guessed instead of simply saying "I'm sad."

qa.q: What did Shankar do to stop the pattern?
qa.a: Shankar noticed it, said plainly that the silence was a punishment, apologised, and promised to ask directly next time.

qa.q: How might Lokesh have experienced the silence?
qa.a: Like walking on eggshells. He looked tired at school and kept apologising, which suggests he felt anxious and unsure of what he had done.

grounding: Shankar catches the habit of punishing Lokesh with silence and guilt, apologises, and decides to ask directly.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Monday
Uma came to see me on her own after the morning assembly. She said she had "done something ugly" in her relationship with Divyansh.
Over the weekend he had gone to his cousin's wedding instead of her dance recital. She didn't reply to his messages for two days, on purpose. When he called, she said, "Fine, I guess I'm not important." She admitted she knew it would make him feel guilty, and that she had done it before.
She said, "My sister calls it passion, but it feels like a trick." I told her that noticing the pattern was the hard part, and asked what she wanted instead. She said, "To just say, 'I was hurt you missed it.'"
We practised saying it aloud. She planned to apologise to Divyansh at lunch today and ask him directly next time. I will check in with her on Friday to see how it went.

qa.q: Why did Divyansh miss Uma's dance recital?
qa.a: He went to his cousin's wedding.

qa.q: What was Uma feeling when she came to the counsellor?
qa.a: She felt guilty and uneasy, calling her silent treatment 'ugly' and a trick she had used before.

qa.q: What steps did the counsellor help Uma take?
qa.a: Noticing the pattern, apologising to Divyansh, and practising a direct way to say she was hurt instead of using silence or guilt.

qa.q: How might Divyansh have felt during Uma's two days of silence?
qa.a: Divyansh probably felt anxious and guilty, confused about what he had done and under pressure to make it up to her.

grounding: A teen notices she uses silent treatment and guilt to get her way, apologises, and learns to ask directly instead.

passage:
Tuesday night
Hemant had to cancel our evening walk because his Nana is in hospital. I knew that. I still wrote, "Wow, okay. Guess I know where I stand." Then I didn't reply to anything he said for hours.
I watched him type, stop, type again. Some part of me, the part Didi calls my drama-queen side, liked it. Like I was winning something.
Then he wrote, "I'm sorry, Himani. I feel bad. I'll make it up." And I felt sick. His Nana is in the ICU, and I made him apologise to me.
I did this last month too, when he went to football. I called it "being passionate." It isn't. It's using guilt to make him do what I want.
Tomorrow I'll tell him, "I'm sorry. That was unfair. I hope your Nana gets better." And next time I'm disappointed, I'll just say, "I'm disappointed, can we plan another day?" Directly. No games.

qa.q: Why did Hemant cancel the evening walk?
What did Himani feel after Hemant apologised?
qa.a: Himani felt sick and ashamed, realising she had made him apologise while his Nana was in the ICU.

qa.q: What is Himani planning to do differently, and why is it better?
qa.a: She plans to apologise and in future say plainly when she is disappointed, instead of using silence and guilt to control him.

qa.q: What is it like for Hemant when Himani goes silent?
qa.a: Hemant probably feels anxious and guilty, trying again and again to type a reply while also worrying about his Nana.

grounding: A teen catches herself using silent treatment and guilt on her boyfriend, names it, and decides to apologise and ask directly.
